eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecast models from European meteorological centers indicate a maximum temperature in Munich on June 1 most likely near 22°C, driven by typical early-summer atmospheric patterns and moderate high-pressure influence. Trader consensus on 21–23°C outcomes reflects this narrow range of model guidance, with lower probabilities assigned to extremes outside historical norms for the period. Updated short-range model runs expected over the next 24 hours will refine the outlook ahead of official observations used for market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current ensemble forecasts from global and regional models place the most likely daytime maximum for Karachi on June 2 in the 35–36 °C range, reflecting typical early-June pre-monsoon heating driven by strong solar insolation and weak steering winds. Historical climatology for the first week of June shows average highs near 34 °C, but recent Pakistan Meteorological Department outlooks note above-normal temperatures persisting into early summer. Model spread arises mainly from uncertainties in boundary-layer moisture and any weak western disturbance that could increase cloud cover or trigger brief showers, trimming peak values by 1–2 °C. With leading probabilities closely matched between 35 °C and 36 °C, traders are weighing the latest high-resolution runs and the urban heat-island amplification typical of the coastal megacity.
